```{python}
#| output: false
import io
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import requests
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_histogram, geom_col, geom_hline, geom_vline, coord_flip,
    labs, theme_minimal,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

LG = "mbb"
SPORT_SLUG = "mens-college-basketball"
DL = "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download"

# The published floor constant lives with the builder; fall back to its value
# when this document is rendered outside the repo tree.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parents[1] / "python"))
try:
    from mbb_model_publish.builders import QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES = 300.0

frames = []
for season in range(2014, 2027):
    r = requests.get(f"{DL}/{LG}_player_value/{LG}_player_value_{season}.parquet", timeout=60)
    if r.status_code == 200:
        frames.append(pl.read_parquet(io.BytesIO(r.content)))
pv = pl.concat(frames, how="diagonal_relaxed")
if "qualified" in pv.columns:
    qualified_src = "the published `qualified` column"
else:
    # Assets published before the flag shipped: derive it identically.
    pv = pv.with_columns((pl.col("min") >= QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES).alias("qualified"))
    qualified_src = f"derived at render time as min >= {QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES:g} (the published frames predate the flag)"
SEASONS = sorted(pv["season"].unique().to_list())
latest = SEASONS[-1]

tb = pl.read_parquet(io.BytesIO(requests.get(
    f"{DL}/espn_{SPORT_SLUG.replace('-', '_')}_team_boxscores/team_box_{latest}.parquet",
    timeout=120).content))
name_col = next(c for c in ("team_display_name", "team_location", "team_name")
                if c in tb.columns)
names = (tb.group_by("team_id").agg(pl.col(name_col).last().alias("team"))
         .with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Int64)))

# The fitted coefficient vector: the release sidecar when published, else the
# same artifact read from the installed sdv-py (what the builder copies).
r = requests.get(f"{DL}/{LG}_player_value/{LG}_player_value_coefficients.json", timeout=60)
if r.status_code == 200:
    art = r.json()
    coef_src = f"the published `{LG}_player_value_coefficients.json` sidecar"
else:
    from sportsdataverse.mbb.mbb_player_value_constants import load_artifact
    art = load_artifact(f"{LG}_box_bpm")
    coef_src = "the bundled sdv-py artifact (the sidecar is not on the release yet)"


def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

Per-player box Plus/Minus publishes on the `mbb_player_value` tag
(`box_obpm` / `box_dbpm` / `box_bpm`): a box-score value model over the
published player/team season stats, sharing the design of the MBB
player-value spine in sdv-py (oracle-gated where trained). Per-100 box
features are standardized and scored through ridge coefficients fit at the
team level, then a uniform team adjustment makes each team's
minutes-weighted player scores sum to its adjusted efficiency margin;
offensive and defensive components are estimated separately and summed.
It is compute-on-demand — every run recomputes from the current published
season assets, so a data correction upstream flows through on the next
publish, and each publish writes a card sidecar plus the fitted coefficient
vector.

Box Plus/Minus and on/off RAPM (the `ncaa_mbb_rapm` model in the NCAA hoops
repos) deliberately measure different things: BPM sees only what reaches the
box score and is therefore stable at small samples but blind to screening,
defensive attention, and everything else the box misses; RAPM sees all of it
but drowns in noise for low-minute players. The two are cross-references,
not substitutes — the natural hybrid (an SPM-prior RAPM, as the NBA impact
suite builds) is the catalogued next step.

Everything below is computed at render time from the published release
assets — the exact frames consumers download.

## Training data

```{python}
tbl = (
    pv.group_by("season")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("players"), pl.col("min").sum().alias("total_minutes"),
         pl.col("qualified").sum().alias("qualified_players"))
    .sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Published mbb_player_value assets, by season",
                subtitle=f"computed at render time from the release; qualified = min >= {QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES:g}")
    .fmt_number(columns=["total_minutes"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
)
```

## Exploratory data analysis

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Box BPM distribution, latest season — the full player pool vs the qualified pool. The unfiltered frame carries heavy low-minute noise by design; the flag marks it, it never removes it."
cur = pv.filter(pl.col("season") == latest)
d = pl.concat([
    cur.select("box_bpm").with_columns(pl.lit("all players").alias("pool")),
    cur.filter(pl.col("qualified") == True).select("box_bpm").with_columns(pl.lit("qualified").alias("pool")),
])
(
    ggplot(d.to_pandas(), aes("box_bpm", fill="pool"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=60, alpha=0.6, position="identity")
    + labs(x="box BPM", y="players", title=f"Player value distribution — {latest}")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Minutes vs |BPM|: with no shrinkage prior, extreme values concentrate at LOW minutes. The vertical line is the qualified floor."
shr = cur.with_columns(pl.col("box_bpm").abs().alias("abs_bpm"))
(
    ggplot(shr.to_pandas(), aes("min", "abs_bpm"))
    + geom_point(alpha=0.1, color="#2a6f97", size=0.6)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + labs(x="minutes", y="|box BPM|",
           title=f"Every player is published; `qualified` marks min >= {QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES:g}")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
edges = [0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 500, 600, 800, 1000, 1400]
labels = [f"{a}-{b}" for a, b in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:])]
fun = (
    pv.with_columns(pl.col("min").cut(edges[1:-1], labels=labels).alias("minutes_bin"))
    .group_by("minutes_bin", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(pl.len().alias("players"), pl.col("box_bpm").std().alias("sd_box_bpm"),
         pl.col("box_bpm").abs().quantile(0.99).alias("abs_bpm_p99"))
    .sort("minutes_bin")
)
plateau = float(fun.filter(pl.col("minutes_bin") == "600-800")["sd_box_bpm"][0])
fun = fun.with_columns((pl.col("sd_box_bpm") / plateau - 1).alias("vs_600_800_plateau"))
gt_show(
    GT(fun.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="How the qualified floor was set — sd(box_bpm) by minutes bin, all published seasons",
                subtitle=f"the floor is the first bin whose sd sits within 10% of the 600–800 plateau ({plateau:.2f}); every table below uses the flag")
    .fmt_number(columns="players", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns=["sd_box_bpm", "abs_bpm_p99"], decimals=2)
    .fmt_percent(columns="vs_600_800_plateau", decimals=0)
)
display(Markdown(f"Flag source in this render: {qualified_src}."))
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Offense vs defense components, qualified players, latest season."
q = cur.filter(pl.col("qualified") == True)
(
    ggplot(q.to_pandas(), aes("box_obpm", "box_dbpm"))
    + geom_point(alpha=0.25, color="#2a6f97", size=0.8)
    + labs(x="offensive BPM", y="defensive BPM", title=f"O/D decomposition — {latest}")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

The minutes-vs-|BPM| funnel is this model's most important consumer-facing
fact, shown rather than footnoted: the published frame keeps **every**
player, so the most extreme values in the file belong to 20-minute seasons.
The additive `qualified` flag encodes the floor the funnel itself justifies —
the bin where the spread of BPM stops shrinking — so a consumer filters with
one boolean instead of re-deriving a threshold. The engine's own fit floor
(`min_minutes` in the artifact) governs only the team-sum weights and is
lower; the two floors answer different questions.

## Coefficient importance

```{python}
cols = art["feature_cols"]
coef = pl.DataFrame({
    "feature": cols,
    "obpm_slope": [float(v) for v in art["obpm_coef"][1:]],
    "dbpm_slope": [float(v) for v in art["dbpm_coef"][1:]],
    "feature_mean": [float(art["feature_mean"][c]) for c in cols],
    "feature_sd": [float(art["feature_sd"][c]) for c in cols],
}).with_columns((pl.col("obpm_slope").abs() + pl.col("dbpm_slope").abs()).alias("abs_total")).sort("abs_total", descending=True)
display(Markdown(
    f"Coefficients from {coef_src}; fit on seasons {art.get('train_seasons')} "
    f"(ridge λ offense {art.get('lambda_o')}, defense {art.get('lambda_d')}; z-clip {art.get('z_clip')}; "
    f"fit floor {art.get('min_minutes')} minutes)."
))
gt_show(
    GT(coef.drop("abs_total").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Fitted box-BPM coefficients (slopes per one SD of the standardized feature)",
                subtitle="intercepts are team-level and absorbed by the team adjustment; |slope| is the BPM moved by one standard deviation of the feature")
    .fmt_number(columns=["obpm_slope", "dbpm_slope"], decimals=3)
    .fmt_number(columns=["feature_mean", "feature_sd"], decimals=4)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Coefficient importance: BPM change per one SD of each standardized per-100 feature, offense and defense."
long = coef.select("feature", "obpm_slope", "dbpm_slope").unpivot(
    index="feature", on=["obpm_slope", "dbpm_slope"], variable_name="component", value_name="slope"
).with_columns(pl.col("component").str.replace("_slope", ""))
order = coef["feature"].to_list()[::-1]
(
    ggplot(long.to_pandas(), aes("feature", "slope", fill="component"))
    + geom_col(position="dodge")
    + geom_hline(yintercept=0, color="gray")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(x="", y="BPM per +1 SD of the feature", title="Box-BPM coefficient importance")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

Because every feature is standardized before scoring, the slopes are
directly comparable: a slope of 2 means one standard deviation of that rate
moves a player's BPM by two points per 100 possessions. Usage and true
shooting dominate offense with opposite signs (volume is penalized until it
is efficient), and points per 100 carries the offensive load; the defensive
vector is smaller and led by the same usage/efficiency pair with the sign
flipped, with rebounding and steals the distinctly defensive contributors.
The vector is republished with every run as
`mbb_player_value_coefficients.json`, alongside the artifact's
standardization moments, so a consumer can reproduce any player's raw score
from the published per-100 features.

## Evaluation

```{python}
qual = pv.filter(pl.col("qualified") == True)
stab = (
    qual.select("player_id", "season", "box_bpm")
    .join(qual.select("player_id", (pl.col("season") - 1).alias("season"),
                      pl.col("box_bpm").alias("next_bpm")),
          on=["player_id", "season"], how="inner")
)
rows = [{"check": "box BPM year-over-year (same player, qualified both seasons)",
         "pairs": stab.height,
         "pearson": float(stab.select(pl.corr("box_bpm", "next_bpm")).item())}]
o_d = qual.filter(pl.col("season") == latest)
rows.append({"check": f"corr(box_obpm, box_dbpm) — {latest}, qualified",
             "pairs": o_d.height,
             "pearson": float(o_d.select(pl.corr("box_obpm", "box_dbpm")).item())})
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame(rows).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Published-asset checks",
                subtitle="YoY reliability is the box model's core virtue; a near-zero O/D correlation means the components carry distinct information")
    .fmt_number(columns="pearson", decimals=3)
)
```

A box model's justification is exactly this reliability: with roster-level
churn as violent as college basketball's, a player metric that persists
season-over-season for returning players is measuring the player. The
engine's own oracle gates (against the sdv-py player-value spine's
references) run where the model is trained.

## Results

```{python}
top = (
    q.sort("box_bpm", descending=True).head(15)
    .with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Int64))
    .join(names, on="team_id", how="left")
    .with_columns(
        ("<img src='https://a.espncdn.com/i/headshots/" + SPORT_SLUG
         + "/players/full/" + pl.col("player_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8)
         + ".png' height='40'/>").alias("headshot"))
)
gt_show(
    GT(top.select("headshot", "player", "team", "min", "box_obpm", "box_dbpm", "box_bpm").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Top 15 box BPM — {latest} (qualified players)")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="headshot")
    .fmt_number(columns="min", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns=["box_obpm", "box_dbpm", "box_bpm"], decimals=2)
    .cols_label(headshot="", player="Player", team="Team", min="Min",
                box_obpm="O-BPM", box_dbpm="D-BPM", box_bpm="BPM")
)
```

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Computed from:** this repository's published player/team season stats
  for the seasons in the corpus table; recomputed in full on every run
  (compute-on-demand — no fitted artifact is stored here).
- **Engine:** the MBB player-value spine in sdv-py (oracle-gated where
  trained); O/D estimated separately and summed. The fitted coefficient
  vector ships with every publish as `mbb_player_value_coefficients.json`
  (features, intercept + slopes on standardized features, moments, λ, fit
  floor, train seasons, sportsdataverse version, artifact sha256).
- **`qualified`:** additive flag, `min >= 300`, set where sd(box_bpm) first
  sits within 10% of its 600–800-minute plateau on the published 2014–2026
  assets (derivation table above; constant `QUALIFIED_MIN_MINUTES` in
  `python/mbb_model_publish/builders.py`, recorded in `models/REGISTRY.md`).
  No row is filtered.
- **Pipeline:** `scripts/mbb_models.sh 02` → stage
  `python/mbb_model_02_player_value.py`; card sidecar
  [`mbb_models_eval_card.json`](mbb_models_eval_card.json). Single home:
  `models/manifest.yaml`.
- **Rebuild this document:** `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM;
  `uv sync --group docs`). Requires network for the release download and the
  ESPN headshot CDN.

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Blend with on/off** — box Plus/Minus and the league-wide RAPM measure
  different things; a stabilized hybrid (SPM-prior RAPM, as the NBA impact
  suite does) is the natural next step.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #25):** the fitted coefficient vector ships
  with every publish as `mbb_player_value_coefficients.json`, and the
  coefficient-importance section above is drawn from it.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #25):** the published frame now carries an
  additive `qualified` flag (`min >= 300`, derived from the funnel's own
  noise curve); low-minute rows are still published, now marked.
